question: State Snell's law of refraction and explain the bending of light when it travels from an optically rarer medium to an optically denser medium. Hence calculate the refractive index of glass if a ray incident at $60^\circ$ is refracted at $35^\circ$.

options.A: Snell's law is $\frac{\sin r}{\sin i}=n$. From air to glass, the ray bends away from the normal. $n=\frac{\sin35^\circ}{\sin60^\circ}\approx0.66$.
options.B: Snell's law is $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}=n_{21}$. From a rarer medium to a denser medium, light slows and bends towards the normal, so $r$n=\frac{\sin60^\circ}{\sin35^\circ}=\frac{0.866}{0.574}\approx1.51$.
options.C: From air to glass, the ray bends away from the normal because its speed decreases. $n=\frac{60^\circ}{35^\circ}\approx1.71$.
options.D: Snell's law states $i=r$ in all media. Hence glass has refractive index $1.0$.
